Clean Cooking: From overlooked issue to global priority

At today’s @UnitedNationsEnergy session on clean cooking, I was delighted to share why the clean cooking imperative must move from the margins of energy discussions to the center of sustainable development.

Every year, household air pollution from dirty cooking fuels causes 6.67 million deaths - more than malaria, tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS combined. The economic costs exceed $2.4 trillion annually, yet clean cooking receives < 1% of global energy investment, far below the $8 billion needed each year to reach universal access by 2030. We’re paying trillions to avoid spending billions.

To reframe this we must:

1️⃣ Integrate clean cooking into electrification planning – as is already happening in Zambia, where e-cooking is part of mini-grid expansion strategies, making entire systems more viable while supporting productive uses like food processing and irrigation.

2️⃣ Unlock innovative finance and market development – as is already happening in Tanzania, where the UNCDF-backed CookFund uses concessional loans and results-based finance to reduce end-user costs by up to 60%, proving that public capital can de-risk private investment and build viable markets.

3️⃣ Harness #digitalization, #AI, and IoT for innovation – as we are already seeing in Kenya, where IoT-enabled smart meters power pay-as-you-go LPG, letting households purchase fuel in $0.50 increments via mobile money, ensuring resilience even during COVID-19 lockdowns.

Momentum is building. The solutions are here. What’s missing is bold finance, political will and collective resolve.
